title: A Pokémon fan game where your Pokémon is an AI agent
author: rocky_racoooon
selftext:
**A Pokémon fan game where your Pokémon is an AI agent**

I wanted to share a fan game my cousin has been working on called **Pokémon Nevatown**.

Nevatown is a platform for creating AI-based games and worlds, and Pokémon Nevatown is one of the games built on it.

The basic idea is a little different from a normal Pokémon game. You don’t control a trainer walking around the map. Instead, you adopt a Pokémon and interact with it directly.

You can talk to your Pokémon in natural language, give it advice, tell it what you want it to do, and it goes around living its own life in the world. It can explore, train, make friends, challenge gyms, battle, etc.

So you’re basically guiding your Pokémon rather than directly controlling it.

https://reddit.com/link/1xmjjwd/video/0n5dyf64sbzh1/player

One part we’ve been working on recently is **AI Arena**, which is a separate system for training how your Pokémon fights.

Battles in Pokémon Nevatown aren’t turn-based. They happen in real time, with movement, positioning, dodging, terrain, weather and the Pokémon’s own behavior all affecting the fight.

The player doesn’t directly control the Pokémon during combat.

https://reddit.com/link/1xmjjwd/video/l2aj6a07sbzh1/player

https://reddit.com/link/1xmjjwd/video/ajxltio7sbzh1/player

Because of that, making your Pokémon stronger isn’t only about leveling up and increasing stats. You can also train its actual battle strategy.

In AI Arena, you can hand your Pokémon to an AI agent and have it run practice battles against other Pokémon. The agent can study what happened, change the strategy, test it again and keep iterating. It can run up to 1,000 practice battles a day before you send the Pokémon onto the ranked ladder.

Personality matters too. A reckless Pokémon might naturally fight more aggressively, for example, so the strategy has to work with the Pokémon rather than every Pokémon behaving the same way.

The part I find especially interesting is that the strategy trained in AI Arena carries back into the main game.

So if your agent figures out a better way for your Pokémon to fight, that becomes how it fights in wild battles, gyms, raids, etc.

That’s probably the biggest thing we’ve been experimenting with from the AI side: using AI as part of the actual gameplay and progression, rather than just putting an LLM behind NPC dialogue.

There’s also an interesting design problem around how much autonomy to give the Pokémon. It needs enough independence to feel like its own character, but the player still needs to feel like the way they raise and train it matters.
